17: function stripIgnored(src) {
18:   let out = "";
19:   let i = 0;
20:   const n = src.length;
21:   while (i < n) {
22:     const c = src[i], c2 = src[i + 1];
23:     if (c === "/" && c2 === "/") { while (i < n && src[i] !== "\n") i++; continue; }
24:     if (c === "/" && c2 === "*") { i += 2; while (i < n && !(src[i] === "*" && src[i + 1] === "/")) i++; i += 2; continue; }
25:     if (c === '"' || c === "'" || c === "`") {
26:       const q = c; out += c; i++;
27:       while (i < n) {
28:         if (src[i] === "\\") { out += src[i]; if (i + 1 < n) out += src[i + 1]; i += 2; continue; }
29:         if (src[i] === q) { out += src[i]; i++; break; }
30:         out += src[i]; i++;
31:       }
32:       continue;
33:     }
34:     out += c; i++;
35:   }
36:   return out;
37: }

39: function findCallsByName(code, name) {
40:   const sanitized = stripIgnored(code);
41:   const calls = [];
42:   const re = new RegExp("\\b" + name + "\\b", "g");
43:   const idxs = [];
44:   let m;
45:   while ((m = re.exec(sanitized)) !== null) idxs.push(m.index + m[0].length);
46:   for (const start of idxs) {
47:     let i = start;
48:     while (i < sanitized.length && sanitized[i] !== "(") i++;
49:     if (sanitized[i] !== "(") continue;
50:     let depth = 0, argStart = i + 1; const args = [];
51:     for (let j = i; j < sanitized.length; j++) {
52:       const ch = sanitized[j];
53:       if (ch === "(") depth++;
54:       else if (ch === ")") {
55:         depth--;
56:         if (depth === 0) {
57:           const raw = sanitized.slice(argStart, j);
58:           if (raw.trim().length > 0) args.push(raw);
59:           calls.push(args.map(a => a.trim()).filter(a => a.length > 0));
60:           break;
61:         }
62:       } else if (ch === "," && depth === 1) {
63:         args.push(sanitized.slice(argStart, j));
64:         argStart = j + 1;
65:       }
66:     }
67:   }
68:   return calls;

71: function checkExercise(ex) {
72:   if (!ex.tasks || ex.tasks.length === 0) return;
73:   const finalTask = ex.tasks[ex.tasks.length - 1];
74:   const solution = ex.solution ?? "";
75:   for (let ti = 0; ti < ex.tasks.length; ti++) {
76:     const task = ex.tasks[ti];
77:     for (const rule of task.validation ?? []) {
78:       if (rule.type === "functionCall") {
79:         const calls = findCallsByName(solution, rule.name);
80:         if (calls.length === 0) {
81:           // only a failure if this rule is on the final task (solution = final state)
82:           if (ti === ex.tasks.length - 1) {
83:             console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: solution missing ${rule.name}() call`);
84:             failures++;
85:           }
86:         } else if (rule.exactArgs !== undefined) {
87:           const ok = calls.some(a => a.length === rule.exactArgs);
88:           if (!ok && ti === ex.tasks.length - 1) {
89:             console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: solution ${rule.name}() has ${calls.map(c=>c.length).join(",")} args, expected ${rule.exactArgs}`);
90:             failures++;
91:           }
92:         }
93:       } else if (rule.type === "canvasSize") {
94:         const re = /createCanvas\s*\(\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)\s*\)/;
95:         const mm = re.exec(solution);
96:         if (mm && (parseInt(mm[1]) !== rule.width || parseInt(mm[2]) !== rule.height)) {
97:           if (ti === ex.tasks.length - 1) {
98:             console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: solution canvas ${mm[1]}x${mm[2]}, expected ${rule.width}x${rule.height}`);
99:             failures++;
100:           }
101:         }
102:       } else if (rule.type === "expectedPixels") {
103:         if (!Array.isArray(rule.points) || rule.points.length === 0) {
104:           console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: expectedPixels has no points`);
105:           failures++;
106:         }
107:         if (rule.minPassFraction !== undefined && (rule.minPassFraction < 0 || rule.minPassFraction > 1)) {
108:           console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: expectedPixels minPassFraction out of [0,1]`);
109:           failures++;
110:         }
111:         for (const p of rule.points ?? []) {
112:           if (!Array.isArray(p.expected) || p.expected.length !== 3) {
113:             console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: expectedPixels point missing expected[3]`);
114:             failures++;
115:           }
116:         }
117:       } else if (rule.type === "pixelMatch") {
118:         if (!Array.isArray(rule.expected) || rule.expected.length !== 3) {
119:           console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: pixelMatch missing expected[3]`);
120:           failures++;
121:         }
122:       }
123:     }
124:   }
125: }

2: // Fetches the latest published p5.js release and regenerates the vendored
3: // source artefacts:

5: //   - src/utils/p5Version.ts  (the resolved version string)

7: // These files are gitignored build artefacts — regenerated on every fresh
8: // install and on `npm start` — so the app always bundles the newest p5.js.
9: // The format of p5Source.ts intentionally mirrors the original hand-authored
10: // shape (`const _p = [ ... ]; export const p5Source = _p.join("")`).

12: import fs from "fs";
13: import https from "https";
14: import path from "path";
15: import { fileURLToPath } from "url";
16: 
17: const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
18: const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, "..");
19: const P5_SOURCE_FILE = path.join(ROOT, "src/utils/p5Source.ts");
20: const P5_VERSION_FILE = path.join(ROOT, "src/utils/p5Version.ts");
21: 
22: function fetchText(url, redirects = 0) {
23:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
24:     if (redirects > 10) return reject(new Error("Too many redirects"));
25:     https.get(url, { headers: { "User-Agent": "learn-p5-bundler" } }, (res) => {
26:       if (res.statusCode >= 300 && res.statusCode < 400 && res.headers.location) {
27:         res.resume();
28:         return resolve(fetchText(res.headers.location, redirects + 1));
29:       }
30:       if (res.statusCode !== 200) {
31:         res.resume();
32:         return reject(new Error(`HTTP ${res.statusCode} for ${url}`));
33:       }
34:       const chunks = [];
35:       res.setEncoding("utf8");
36:       res.on("data", (c) => chunks.push(c));
37:       res.on("end", () => resolve(chunks.join("")));
38:       res.on("error", reject);
39:     }).on("error", reject);
40:   });
41: }
42: 
43: async function getLatestVersion() {
44:   const txt = await fetchText("https://registry.npmjs.org/p5/latest");
45:   const data = JSON.parse(txt);
46:   if (!data.version) throw new Error("No version field in npm registry response");
47:   return data.version;
48: }
49: 
50: function escapeForDoubleQuotedString(s) {
51:   // We emit the source as a JS double-quoted string literal. Escape in an
52:   // order that avoids double-escaping: backslashes first, then real control
53:   // chars that would otherwise break the literal across lines, then quotes.
54:   return s
55:     .replace(/\\/g, "\\\\")
56:     .replace(/\r/g, "\\r")
57:     .replace(/\n/g, "\\n")
58:     .replace(/"/g, '\\"');
59: }
60: 
61: // Split the (potentially huge) minified source into a few array elements so
62: // the generated file stays diff-friendly and avoids pathological single-line
63: // lengths that choke some tooling.
64: function chunkSource(src, chunkSize = 200_000) {
65:   const chunks = [];
66:   for (let i = 0; i < src.length; i += chunkSize) {
67:     chunks.push(src.slice(i, i + chunkSize));
68:   }
69:   return chunks;
70: }
71: 
72: function writeP5Source(version, src) {
73:   const escaped = chunkSource(src).map((c) => `"${escapeForDoubleQuotedString(c)}"`);
74:   const body = escaped.join(",\n  ");
75:   const file =
76:     `// AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/bundle-p5.mjs — do not edit directly.\n` +
77:     `// p5.js v${version} — fetched from the npm registry (latest) at build time.\n` +
78:     `// Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/p5@${version}/lib/p5.min.js\n\n` +
79:     `const _p = [\n  ${body}\n];\n\n` +
80:     `export const p5Source: string = _p.join("");\n`;
81:   fs.writeFileSync(P5_SOURCE_FILE, file, "utf-8");
82: }
83: 
84: function writeP5Version(version) {
85:   const file =
86:     `// AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/bundle-p5.mjs — do not edit directly.\n` +
87:     `export const p5Version = "${version}";\n`;
88:   fs.writeFileSync(P5_VERSION_FILE, file, "utf-8");
89: }
90: 
91: async function main() {
92:   const version = await getLatestVersion();
93:   console.log(`[bundle-p5] Latest p5.js version: ${version}`);
94:   const url = `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/p5@${version}/lib/p5.min.js`;
95:   console.log(`[bundle-p5] Fetching ${url}`);
96:   const src = await fetchText(url);
97:   if (!src || src.length < 100_000) {
98:     throw new Error(`Fetched p5 source looks empty/too small (${src?.length ?? 0} bytes)`);
99:   }
100:   writeP5Source(version, src);
101:   writeP5Version(version);
102:   console.log(`[bundle-p5] Wrote ${P5_SOURCE_FILE} (${src.length} bytes)`);
103:   console.log(`[bundle-p5] Wrote ${P5_VERSION_FILE}`);
104: }
105: 
106: main().catch((err) => {
107:   console.error("[bundle-p5] FAILED:", err);
108:   process.exit(1);
109: });

# loadImage()

Loads an image to create a [p5.Image](/reference/p5/p5.Image) object.

`loadImage()` interprets the first parameter one of three ways. If the path to an image file is provided, `loadImage()` will load it. Paths to local files should be relative, such as `'/assets/thundercat.jpg'`. URLs such as `'https://example.com/thundercat.jpg'` may be blocked due to browser security. Raw image data can also be passed as a base64 encoded image in the form `'data:image/png;base64,arandomsequenceofcharacters'`. The `path` parameter can also be defined as a `Request` object for more advanced usage.

The second parameter is optional. If a function is passed, it will be called once the image has loaded. The callback function can optionally use the new [p5.Image](/reference/p5/p5.Image) object. The return value of the function will be used as the final return value of `loadImage()`.

The third parameter is also optional. If a function is passed, it will be called if the image fails to load. The callback function can optionally use the event error. The return value of the function will be used as the final return value of `loadImage()`.

This function returns a `Promise` and should be used in an `async` setup with `await`. See the examples for the usage syntax.

## Examples

## Syntax

`loadImage(path, [successCallback], [failureCallback])  `

## Parameters

path

String|Request: path of the image to be loaded or base64 encoded image.

successCallback

function(p5.Image): function called with [p5.Image](/reference/p5/p5.Image/) once it loads.

failureCallback

function(Event): function called with event error if the image fails to load.

## Returns

Promise<p5.Image>: the [p5.Image](/reference/p5/p5.Image/) object.

# bezierVertex()

Adds a Bézier curve segment to a custom shape.

`bezierVertex()` adds a curved segment to custom shapes. The Bézier curves it creates are defined like those made by the [bezier()](/reference/p5/bezier/) function. `bezierVertex()` must be called between the [beginShape()](/reference/p5/beginShape/) and [endShape()](/reference/p5/endShape/) functions. Bézier need a starting point. Building a shape only with Bézier curves needs one initial call to [bezierVertex()](/reference/p5/vertex/), before a number of `bezierVertex()` calls that is a multiple of the parameter set by [bezierOrder(...)](/reference/p5/bezierOrder/) (default 3). But shapes can mix different types of vertices, so if there are some previous vertices, then the initial anchor is not needed, only the multiples of 3 (or the Bézier order) calls to `bezierVertex` for each curve.

Each curve of order 3 requires three calls to `bezierVertex`, so 2 curves would need 7 calls to `bezierVertex()`: (1 one initial anchor point, two sets of 3 curves describing the curves) With `bezierOrder(2)`, two curves would need 5 calls: 1 + 2 + 2.

Bézier curves can also be drawn in 3D using WebGL mode.

Note: `bezierVertex()` won’t work when an argument is passed to [beginShape()](/reference/p5/beginShape/).

`bezierVertex(x, y, [u], [v])  ``bezierVertex(x, y, z, [u], [v])  `

I've completed a thorough audit. Here's what I found before asking clarifying questions.

## Audit findings

**The three code-level asks:**

1. **Target Solution auto-run** — Currently `solution-content` renders expanded by default (exerciseHtml.ts:382) and only runs when the inline "Run" button is tapped (exerciseHtml.ts:1416-1434). I'll collapse it by default and auto-run on expand.

2. **Long press** — The Run button uses a custom 600ms timer (`.tsx:589`). React Native's default long-press is **500ms**. I'll change it to 500ms.

3. **Exercise content audit** — I reviewed all 16 course YAMLs and found these concrete bugs:

**Definite logic/visual bugs (solution or rules can't pass / don't render):**
- `shapes/exercise-1`: solution fills **orange** but task-1 pixelMatch expects **pink** (task-2 changes color — single-solution-vs-multi-task mismatch)
- `shapes/exercise-3`: solution is a 300×300 circle, task-1 asks for 300×150 ellipse
- `shapes/exercise-4`: task-2 says "you now have two line() calls creating an X" but the solution has only **one** line()
- `events/exercise-1`: circles drawn in `mousePressed()` are wiped by `background()` every frame — clicks never persist visually
- `image/exercise-3`: GRAY filter on pure red gives ~**54** (CIE luminance 0.2126·255), but pixelMatch expects **[126,126,126]** → task always fails
- `math/exercise-5`: `expectedPixels` at 4 cardinal points with `minPassFraction: 0.9` can **never pass** (orbiting circle is at one point per frame)
- `random-noise/exercise-4`: `frameCount` is validated as a *function call* (impossible — it's a property), and task-2 requires `noise` with `minArgs: 2` while the solution calls `noise(frameCount * 0.01)` with **1** arg → both tasks always fail
- `custom-shapes/exercise-3`: uses 6-arg `bezierVertex(x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3)` — **p5 v1 syntax**. The app bundles p5 v2.3.x where `bezierVertex(x, y)` is a single-point call (multiples of `bezierOrder`, default 3). The blob won't render.
- `io/exercise-2`: `img = loadImage(url)` returns a **Promise** in p5 v2 → `image(img, …)` breaks; needs `async setup` + `await`
- `vectors/exercise-2`: `(300,100).sub(100,200).mult(1.5)` = **(300, −150)** — circle drawn off-canvas, invisible

**Fragile / needs device verification:**
- `transform/exercise-1`: pixel sampled at (150,150) — exactly on the rect's black stroke corner → may fail
- `curves/exercise-2`: spline pixelMatch at (200,180) — unverified point on the curve
- `random-noise/exercise-1`: pixel depends on seeded circle overlap; also task-2 asks to "add randomSeed(42)" already present in starter
- `math/exercise-3`: pixelMatch at (200,200) flaky since circle follows the mouse
- `io` course: relies on external URLs (jsonplaceholder, picsum, github raw) — may be blocked/offline in WebView

**Requires the generated reference to verify:** whether every function used in courses (splineVertex, bezierTangent, orbitControl, etc.) exists in `P5_FUNCTION_NAMES` so keyboard quick-keys, tap-to-ref, and instruction highlighting work.

Since I'm in plan mode and this affects a lot of content, let me clarify a few key decisions:

options.description: Keep one solution; only fix contradictions where the final-state solution violates its own rules (e.g. shapes/ex-4 missing line). Accept that earlier tasks' preview won't match.

options.description: Runs the solution every time it's expanded; keep the small Replay button for re-running animated solutions.

## Goal
- In learn-p5 (v0.6.118, Expo/p5.js learning app): (1) collapse Target Solution by default and auto-run it when the preview pane is first expanded; (2) use the default long-press duration for the Run sketch button (currently a custom 600ms timer → RN default 500ms); (3) audit/fix all 16 course YAMLs so solutions make sense both as code and visually, and verify publicly used module symbols exist in the reference.

## Constraints & Preferences
- User confirmed (via Q&A): per-task `solution` fields (exercise-level solution = final task); auto-run the Target Solution on every expand, keep the Replay button; bundle local data URIs for `io` course (offline-safe); verify every YAML-used function against the reference and add a check script; fix all confirmed + fragile bugs across all 16 courses in this pass.
- AGENTS.md: edit only `src/data/courses/*.yaml`; generated `.ts`/`reference.generated.json`/`p5Source.ts` are gitignored build artifacts; after YAML edits run `npm run build-courses` then `npm run check-exercises`.
- Never run `npm install` on the dev machine (node_modules absent — build/check scripts cannot run locally right now).
- Push to `main` requires version bump + tag: `sh scripts/bump-version.sh` → commit `vX.Y.Z: <subject>` → tag → push both.

## Progress
### Done
- Explored app structure: `src/app/learn/[course]/[id].tsx` (exercise screen), `src/utils/editor/exerciseHtml.ts` (editor WebView), `src/utils/editor/fullscreenPreviewHtml.ts`, `src/data/courses/*.yaml` (16 files), `src/data/types.ts`, `scripts/check-exercises.mjs`.
- Confirmed p5 bundled latest is 2.3.x (npm latest = 2.3.2); v2 API changes verified via web: `bezierVertex(x, y)` is now a single control-point call (multiples of `bezierOrder`, default 3) — old 6-arg syntax removed; `loadImage()` returns a Promise (needs `await` in async setup); `splineVertex` is the v2 rename of `curveVertex`; `loadImage` supports base64 `data:` URIs.
- Full audit of all 16 course YAMLs; found concrete bugs (see Critical Context).

### In Progress
- (none)

### Blocked
- Running `npm run build-courses`, `npm run check-exercises`, `npm run gen-reference` locally — no `node_modules` installed (per AGENTS.md the user handles installation).

## Key Decisions

49:     if (sanitized[i] !== "(") continue;
50:     let depth = 0, argStart = i + 1; const args = [];
51:     for (let j = i; j < sanitized.length; j++) {
52:       const ch = sanitized[j];
53:       if (ch === "(") depth++;
54:       else if (ch === ")") {
55:         depth--;
56:         if (depth === 0) {
57:           const raw = sanitized.slice(argStart, j);
58:           if (raw.trim().length > 0) args.push(raw);
59:           calls.push(args.map(a => a.trim()).filter(a => a.length > 0));
60:           break;
61:         }
62:       } else if (ch === "," && depth === 1) {
63:         args.push(sanitized.slice(argStart, j));
64:         argStart = j + 1;
65:       }
66:     }
67:   }
68:   return calls;
69: }

71: function checkExercise(ex) {
72:   if (!ex.tasks || ex.tasks.length === 0) return;
73:   const finalTask = ex.tasks[ex.tasks.length - 1];
74:   const solution = ex.solution ?? "";
75:   for (let ti = 0; ti < ex.tasks.length; ti++) {
76:     const task = ex.tasks[ti];
77:     for (const rule of task.validation ?? []) {
78:       if (rule.type === "functionCall") {
79:         const calls = findCallsByName(solution, rule.name);
80:         if (calls.length === 0) {

82:           if (ti === ex.tasks.length - 1) {
83:             console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: solution missing ${rule.name}() call`);
84:             failures++;
85:           }
86:         } else if (rule.exactArgs !== undefined) {
87:           const ok = calls.some(a => a.length === rule.exactArgs);
88:           if (!ok && ti === ex.tasks.length - 1) {
89:             console.error(`  ✗ ${ex.id}/${task.id}: solution ${rule.name}() has ${calls.map(c=>c.length).join(",")} args, expected ${rule.exactArgs}`);

# filter()

Applies an image filter to the image.

The preset options are:

`INVERT` Inverts the colors in the image. No parameter is used.

`GRAY` Converts the image to grayscale. No parameter is used.

`THRESHOLD` Converts the image to black and white. Pixels with a grayscale value above a given threshold are converted to white. The rest are converted to black. The threshold must be between 0.0 (black) and 1.0 (white). If no value is specified, 0.5 is used.

`OPAQUE` Sets the alpha channel to be entirely opaque. No parameter is used.

`POSTERIZE` Limits the number of colors in the image. Each color channel is limited to the number of colors specified. Values between 2 and 255 are valid, but results are most noticeable with lower values. The default value is 4.

`BLUR` Blurs the image.
The level of blurring is specified by a blur radius. Larger values increase the blur. The default value is 4. A gaussian blur is used in `P2D` mode. A box blur is used in `WEBGL` mode.

`ERODE` Reduces the light areas. No parameter is used.

`DILATE` Increases the light areas. No parameter is used.

# color-luminance

[stable](http://github.com/badges/stability-badges)

Functions for calculating the relative luminance of a RGB color.
Since this is just a weighted sum, you can pass components in the range
0-255 or 0-1.

```js
var luminance = require('color-luminance');

//example for RGB inputs in the range 0-255
var Y = luminance(255, 25, 125);

//or with RGB arrays
var Y = luminance([ 255, 25, 125 ]);
```

## coefficients

The exported function uses the [Rec. 601 standard](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rec.
_601) for coefficients (used in most digital video formats).

More details [here](http://haugk.co.uk/2012/11/22/luma-rec-601-vs-rec-709/) .

You can instead use the more explicit functions like so, depending on your needs:

```js
var luminance = require('color-luminance');

//Uses Rec. 709 (HDTV) coefficients

var y1 = luminance.rec709(r, g, b);

//Uses Rec. 601 (PAL/NTSC) coefficients
//R * 0.299 + G * 0.587 + B * 0.114
var y2 = luminance.rec601(r, g, b);
```

In photography and computing , a **grayscale** or **greyscale** digital image is an image in which the value of each pixel is a single sample") , that is, it carries only intensity information. The TIFF and the PNG (among other) image file formats support 16-bit grayscale natively, although browsers and many imaging programs tend to ignore the low order 8 bits of each pixel.

No matter what pixel depth is used, the binary representations assume that 0 is black and the maximum value (255 at 8 bpp, 65,535 at 16 bpp, etc.) is white, if not otherwise noted.

## Converting color to grayscale

Conversion of a color image to grayscale is not unique; different weighting of the color channels effectively represent the effect of shooting black-and-white film with different-colored photographic filters on the cameras.

### Colorimetric (luminance-preserving) conversion to grayscale

A common strategy is to use the principles of photometry") or, more broadly, colorimetry to match the luminance") of the grayscale image to the luminance of the original color image.

22: function fetchText(url, redirects = 0) {

25:     https.get(url, { headers: { "User-Agent": "learn-p5-bundler" } }, (res) => {
26:       if (res.statusCode >= 300 && res.statusCode < 400 && res.headers.location) {
27:         res.resume();

32:         return reject(new Error(`HTTP ${res.statusCode} for ${url}`));
33:       }
34:       const chunks = [];
35:       res.setEncoding("utf8");
36:       res.on("data", (c) => chunks.push(c));
37:       res.on("end", () => resolve(chunks.join("")));
38:       res.on("error", reject);

50: function escapeForDoubleQuotedString(s) {
51:   // We emit the source as a JS double-quoted string literal. Escape in an
52:   // order that avoids double-escaping: backslashes first, then real control
53:   // chars that would otherwise break the literal across lines, then quotes.
54:   return s
55:     .replace(/\\/g, "\\\\")
56:     .replace(/\r/g, "\\r")

62: // the generated file stays diff-friendly and avoids pathological single-line
63: // lengths that choke some tooling.
64: function chunkSource(src, chunkSize = 200_000) {
65:   const chunks = [];
66:   for (let i = 0; i < src.length; i += chunkSize) {
67:     chunks.push(src.slice(i, i + chunkSize));
68:   }
69:   return chunks;

- **D — `shapes.yaml` (partial):** added per-task solutions: ex-1 task-1 (pink circle), ex-1 task-2 (orange circle), ex-2 task-1 (rect 100,100,200,200). # beginShape()

Begins adding vertices to a custom shape.

The `beginShape()` and endShape() functions allow for creating custom shapes in 2D or 3D. `beginShape()` begins adding vertices to a custom shape and endShape() stops adding them.

The parameter, `kind` , sets the kind of shape to make. By default, any irregular polygon can be drawn. The available modes for kind are:

* `POINTS` to draw a series of points.
* `LINES` to draw a series of unconnected line segments.
* `TRIANGLES` to draw a series of separate triangles.
* `TRIANGLE_FAN` to draw a series of connected triangles sharing the first vertex in a fan-like fashion.

* `QUADS` to draw a series of separate quadrilaterals (quads).
* `QUAD_STRIP` to draw quad strip using adjacent edges to form the next quad.
* `TESS` to create a filling curve by explicit tessellation (WebGL only).

Transformations such as translate() , rotate() , and scale() don't work between `beginShape()` and endShape() . It's also not possible to use other shapes, such as ellipse() or rect() , between `beginShape()` and endShape() .

# `bezierVertex()`

The bezierVertex() function in p5.js allows you to create smooth curves by defining control points for your shapes. This is particularly useful in creative coding when you want to draw complex, organic shapes or paths that aren't easily achieved with straight lines. For example, in a fantasy RPG sketch, you can create winding paths or flowing landscapes that captivate the viewer's imagination.

[📖 p5.js Reference →](https://p5js.org/reference/p5/bezierVertex/)
## 🧠 See The Whole Picture

Think of the canvas as a blank piece of paper. The bezierVertex() function plants a pen at the current position, then draws a smooth curve toward the specified endpoint, shaped by the control points, much like how a pen glides across the paper following your hand's motion.

## 📖 Visual Learner's Guide

#### The Big Picture:

When you run this code, you would see a smooth curve drawn on the canvas, creating an elegant shape that flows gracefully.

#### Visual Analogy:

Imagine drawing a winding river with a flexible straw. The end of the straw is where the river flows to, while the bends of the straw shape the river's path.

#### The Numbers Decoded:

For example, if x1=200, it means the curve ends 200 pixels from the left edge of the canvas, while y1=150 means it ends 150 pixels down from the top. The control points shape the curve's flow.

#### Connection Map:
Just like how fill() colors the inside of a shape and stroke() defines its outline, bezierVertex() creates the shape's outline based on your control points.

#### Common Gotcha:

Many beginners forget that bezierVertex() requires a previous vertex to draw from. Without starting with a vertex, the curve cannot be created!

## 🔄 How It Works

## 📝 Syntax

### 📖 How to Read This

Read bezierVertex(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3) as: 'Draw a curve from the current position to the point defined by (x1, y1) using control points (x2, y2) and (x3, y3) to shape the curve. The parentheses hold the necessary info to create the curve, like a recipe book for baking a cake.'

```
bezierVertex(param1, param2, ...)
```

**Example:** `bezierVertex(200, 150, 80)`

### 🔀 Different Ways to Call It
`bezierVertex(value)` 

This form is used when you want to create a simple curve with a single control point.

`bezierVertex(128)` → This will create a minimal curve, showing how even a single point can alter the shape. 

`bezierVertex(v1, v2, v3)` 

This form is used when you want to define a curve with multiple control points.

`bezierVertex(255, 100, 50)` → This will produce a more complex curve that can create dynamic shapes. 

### ↩️ What It Returns

**Type:** `void`

The bezierVertex() function does not return any value; it directly modifies the shape on the canvas, like a painter applying strokes to a blank canvas.

### 🎛️ Mode-Dependent Behavior

The bezierVertex() function behaves consistently across color modes, but its visual output can change based on stroke and fill settings.

#### 📥 What Goes In

You provide bezierVertex() with a series of numbers. The first two are like a destination point - they tell WHERE to end the curve.
The next points are like guiding hands that shape how the curve moves toward that destination.

#### 📤 What Happens

When you call bezierVertex(), it takes your input and draws a smooth curve on the canvas. It follows the active stroke color for the outline and fills the shape with the current fill color, creating a visually appealing path.

### Parameters

`x1` Number required 

A Number represents any digit, like 100 or -50\. Think of it as a coordinate on a grid.

This controls the ending point of the curve. Typical values are based on your canvas size. A value of 0 would be at the left edge, while max values (like 400 on a 400px wide canvas) would be at the right edge.

**Range:** 0 to canvas width/height

**Examples:** `0` → Curve starts from the left edge. `200` → Curve is centered. `400` → Curve ends at the right edge. 

#### 💡 How Parameters Work Together

Imagine you're shaping a piece of clay.
The end point (x1, y1) is where you want the clay to end up, while the control points guide how the clay flows and bends. The smoother the control points are set, the more fluid your shape will appear.

The Bézier curves it creates are defined like those made by the bezier() function. bezierVertex() must be called between the beginShape() and endShape() functions. Bézier need a starting point. Building a shape only with Bézier curves needs one initial call to bezierVertex(), before a number of bezierVertex() calls that is a multiple of the parameter set by bezierOrder(...) (default 3). But shapes can mix different types of vertices, so if there are some previous vertices, then the initial anchor is not needed, only the multiples of 3 (or the Bézier order) calls to bezierVertex for each curve.Each curve of order 3 requires three calls to bezierVertex, so 2 curves would need 7 calls to bezierVertex(): (1 one initial anchor point, two sets of 3 curves describing the curves) With bezierOrder(2), two curves would need 5 calls: 1 + 2 + 2.Bézier curves can also be drawn in 3D using WebGL mode.Note: bezierVertex() won’t work when an argument is passed to beginShape().ExamplesSyntax

2: // Fetches the latest published p5.js release and regenerates the vendored
3: // source artefacts:
4: //   - src/utils/p5Source.ts   (the minified p5 library as a string literal)
5: //   - src/utils/p5Version.ts  (the resolved version string)
6: //
7: // These files are gitignored build artefacts — regenerated on every fresh
8: // install and on `npm start` — so the app always bundles the newest p5.js.
9: // The format of p5Source.ts intentionally mirrors the original hand-authored
10: // shape (`const _p = [ ... ]; export const p5Source = _p.join("")`).
11: 
12: import fs from "fs";
13: import https from "https";
14: import path from "path";
15: import { fileURLToPath } from "url";
16: 
17: const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
18: const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, "..");
19: const P5_SOURCE_FILE = path.join(ROOT, "src/utils/p5Source.ts");
20: const P5_VERSION_FILE = path.join(ROOT, "src/utils/p5Version.ts");
21: 
22: function fetchText(url, redirects = 0) {
23:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
24:     if (redirects > 10) return reject(new Error("Too many redirects"));
25:     https.get(url, { headers: { "User-Agent": "learn-p5-bundler" } }, (res) => {
26:       if (res.statusCode >= 300 && res.statusCode < 400 && res.headers.location) {
27:         res.resume();
28:         return resolve(fetchText(res.headers.location, redirects + 1));
29:       }
30:       if (res.statusCode !== 200) {
31:         res.resume();
32:         return reject(new Error(`HTTP ${res.statusCode} for ${url}`));
33:       }
34:       const chunks = [];
35:       res.setEncoding("utf8");
36:       res.on("data", (c) => chunks.push(c));
37:       res.on("end", () => resolve(chunks.join("")));
38:       res.on("error", reject);
39:     }).on("error", reject);
40:   });
41: }
42: 
43: async function getLatestVersion() {
44:   const txt = await fetchText("https://registry.npmjs.org/p5/latest");
45:   const data = JSON.parse(txt);
46:   if (!data.version) throw new Error("No version field in npm registry response");
47:   return data.version;
48: }
49: 
50: function escapeForDoubleQuotedString(s) {
51:   // We emit the source as a JS double-quoted string literal. Escape in an
52:   // order that avoids double-escaping: backslashes first, then real control
53:   // chars that would otherwise break the literal across lines, then quotes.
54:   return s
55:     .replace(/\\/g, "\\\\")
56:     .replace(/\r/g, "\\r")
57:     .replace(/\n/g, "\\n")
58:     .replace(/"/g, '\\"');
59: }
60: 
61: // Split the (potentially huge) minified source into a few array elements so
62: // the generated file stays diff-friendly and avoids pathological single-line
63: // lengths that choke some tooling.
64: function chunkSource(src, chunkSize = 200_000) {
65:   const chunks = [];
66:   for (let i = 0; i < src.length; i += chunkSize) {
67:     chunks.push(src.slice(i, i + chunkSize));
68:   }
69:   return chunks;
70: }
71: 
72: function writeP5Source(version, src) {
73:   const escaped = chunkSource(src).map((c) => `"${escapeForDoubleQuotedString(c)}"`);
74:   const body = escaped.join(",\n  ");
75:   const file =
76:     `// AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/bundle-p5.mjs — do not edit directly.\n` +
77:     `// p5.js v${version} — fetched from the npm registry (latest) at build time.\n` +
78:     `// Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/p5@${version}/lib/p5.min.js\n\n` +
79:     `const _p = [\n  ${body}\n];\n\n` +
80:     `export const p5Source: string = _p.join("");\n`;
81:   fs.writeFileSync(P5_SOURCE_FILE, file, "utf-8");
82: }
83: 
84: function writeP5Version(version) {
85:   const file =
86:     `// AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/bundle-p5.mjs — do not edit directly.\n` +
87:     `export const p5Version = "${version}";\n`;
88:   fs.writeFileSync(P5_VERSION_FILE, file, "utf-8");
89: }
90: 
91: async function main() {
92:   const version = await getLatestVersion();
93:   console.log(`[bundle-p5] Latest p5.js version: ${version}`);
94:   const url = `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/p5@${version}/lib/p5.min.js`;
95:   console.log(`[bundle-p5] Fetching ${url}`);
96:   const src = await fetchText(url);
97:   if (!src || src.length < 100_000) {
98:     throw new Error(`Fetched p5 source looks empty/too small (${src?.length ?? 0} bytes)`);
99:   }
100:   writeP5Source(version, src);
101:   writeP5Version(version);
102:   console.log(`[bundle-p5] Wrote ${P5_SOURCE_FILE} (${src.length} bytes)`);
103:   console.log(`[bundle-p5] Wrote ${P5_VERSION_FILE}`);
104: }
105: 
106: main().catch((err) => {
107:   console.error("[bundle-p5] FAILED:", err);
108:   process.exit(1);
109: });
